key_insight: A hard-trace first-order PINN-style formulation can solve coupled Stokes-Brinkman-Darcy flow while enforcing interface and boundary physics exactly and correcting pressure through integral mass balance.
engineering_relevance: This offers a physics-consistent surrogate for multi-domain flow problems in filtration, porous media, and free-flow coupling where accurate stresses, fluxes, and pressure are critical.
method: Mixed first-order variables for stress, Darcy flux, and pressure gradient avoid second derivatives.
Shared interface traces and boundary liftings enforce kinematic conditions exactly; hard traction constraints impose force balance.
Pressure is corrected after training using an integral momentum relation, without reference-pressure labels.
evidence_signal: Across two manufactured solutions and three permeabilities, mean corrected upper-pressure relative L2 error ranged from 0.87% to 2.58%, and correction improved both upper-pressure L2 and full Brinkman-pressure H1 errors in every run.
watch_item: The approach relies on carefully designed trace sharing, traction constraints, and post-training pressure correction, which may add implementation complexity and sensitivity in more irregular geometries or boundary setups.
paper_title: Hard-Trace First-Order Residual Learning for Coupled Stokes-Brinkman-Darcy Flow
